author: Columbia Standard
title: Senate Judiciary Committee hears concerns over Emil J. Bove III nomination
text:
Lindsey Graham - Ranking Member on the Senate Committee on the Judiciary | Official U.S. Senate headshot
Lindsey Graham - Ranking Member on the Senate Committee on the Judiciary | Official U.S. Senate headshot
U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin, representing Illinois and serving as the Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, delivered an opening statement during a hearing focused on five judicial nominations. The nominees under consideration included Emil J. Bove III for the United States Circuit Judge for the Third Circuit; Edward L. Artau for the United States District Judge for the Southern District of Florida; Kyle Christopher Dudek, Jordan Emery Pratt, and Anne-Leigh Gaylord Moe for positions as United States District Judges in the Middle District of Florida.
Durbin expressed concerns about Emil J. Bove III's suitability for a federal judge position with a lifetime appointment due to his past role as President Trump's personal defense attorney.
"For the last four years, before this one, I was Chairman of this Committee," Durbin stated. "We considered 235 judicial nominees that were sent to us by the White House. Those nominees were all approved by this Committee and by the United States Senate. Eighty percent of the nominees received bipartisan roll call support."
He further noted his disagreements with several nominees from President Trump's first administration regarding constitutional interpretation but highlighted Mr. Bove's unique standing among them: "A former personal defense attorney of President Trump, Mr. Bove has led the effort to weaponize the Department of Justice against the President’s enemies."
Durbin accused Mr. Bove of dismissing career federal prosecutors involved in January 6 insurrection cases and ordering investigations into FBI employees associated with these cases.
"Mr. Bove personally intervened to strike a corrupt bargain with New York City Mayor Eric Adams," Durbin claimed, suggesting that charges against Mayor Adams were dropped in exchange for cooperation with immigration policies.
According to Durbin, a whistleblower complaint revealed that Mr. Bove suggested ignoring federal court orders contrary to administration views: "These serious allegations against Mr. Bove came not from the ACLU but from a career Justice Department lawyer who was promoted by the Trump Administration."
Concerns about Mr. Bove's temperament also surfaced: "According to public reporting, Mr. Bove was subject to an internal investigation over his ‘abusive,’ ‘bellicose’ management style while serving as a federal prosecutor in New York."
Durbin criticized how quickly Mr. Bove was nominated without extensive engagement with local senators compared to other vacancies handled by previous administrations.
Finally, he questioned Mr. Bove's ties to New Jersey since he is identified as being from Pennsylvania and not admitted to practice before the court he is nominated for.
"With Mr. Bove, we see a sign of what is to come," Durbin concluded about President Trump's motivations behind such nominations.
